newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: U.S. slams Philippine bid to hike chocolate tariff.
newsitem.headline: U.S. slams Philippine bid to hike chocolate tariff.

text.p: The U.S. ambassador to Manila has leapt to the defence of his country's chocolate interests, warning that a possible tariff hike would be of "serious concern" to Washington.

Ambassador Thomas Hubbard said in a letter to Philippine officials that attempts to raise the tariff on imported chocolates from 10 to 50 percent flew in the face of efforts to liberalise the Philippines' economy.

"The U.S. government strongly supports recent steps by the Philippine government toward comprehensive trade liberalisation," said the letter, released to reporters by the Philippine finance ministry on Wednesday.

"The fact that the (Philippine government's) Tariff Commission is examining a potential increase in tariffs on chocolate confectionary represents a potential step backwards in that liberalisation effort," Hubbard said.
"This would be of serious concern to the U.S. government...," Hubbard said.

Philippine confectioners recently asked the commission to restore the 50 percent tariff, which was reduced to 10 percent on January this year, arguing that they needed protection because of the high cost of their imported ingredients.
The commission has yet to rule on the petition.
The United States exported $10.2 million worth of chocolates to the Philippines last year.
